Maria: heads-up: after yesterday's kernel routing tweak I started seeing transient OOMs on a few 80g nodes when continuous batching kicks in. Not a full crash but evictions + 5–10% tail latency spike.
Tony: hmm, which tweak? the kernel selection change that prefers fused attention kernel for short-seqs?
Maria: yeah that one. Perf looks better overall but KV cache pressure seems to spike for mixed-length workloads. reproducer attached in the perf job: perf-bot posted link
perf-bot: perf run: https://perf.internal/runs/4970006 (profiles + flamegraphs)
Devin: quick scan: flame shows big memcpy spikes during KV restore path, and the batching window is forming batches with long prefix + ~10 short inlines -> big KV footprint on restore.
Linh: can you paste the batch formation log? want to see token budgets + allocator signals.
Maria: paste:
```
[batch-alloc] window=12ms budget_target=1024 tokens_est=1890 kv_est=742MB headroom_remain=120MB
[queue-alloc] admitted=8 pending=3 reason=kv_headroom_low
```
Devin: looks like we overshoot because budget_target is per-batch not per-request. If requests have KV footprints we need per-request token->kv heuristics.
Tony: proposal: add a lightweight estimator at admission time that computes kv_delta = request.kv_len_est * kv_token_ratio and reject/admit accordingly. Also lower budget_target when per-gpu-kv_util > 70%.
Maria: agreed but need safe defaults to avoid throughput cliff. maybe a soft-reject that demotes members to a low-KV queue instead of outright deny.
Linh: sketch of admission pseudocode:
```
for req in queue:
  est_kv = req.tokens * EST_KV_PER_TOKEN
  if gpu_kv_used + est_kv > GPU_KV_LIMIT - SAFETY_MARGIN:
    move req -> low_kv_queue
  else:
    admit(req)
```
Where low_kv_queue has stricter token caps and triggers kernel route that avoids big KV restore (fallback to kernel B).
Devin: we should also tune EST_KV_PER_TOKEN per model/seq-dist from recent traces; the perf run has per-model histograms.
Maria: perf run shows model=redwood-open-16k has kv_ratio ~0.28 for long prefix traces, but short chat seqs have 0.05.
Tony: operationally: add two controls:
- kv_admit_threshold_pct (default 85%)
- low_kv_queue_token_cap (default 128)
so we can A/B with feature flags.
Linh: will add a debug metric kv_admit_moved_count and kv_admit_reject_count. also emit sample of moved requests (ids) for replay.
Maria: quick check: do we need kernel selection change? maybe route low_kv_queue to fused kernel but avoid KV restore path by instructing runtime to use streaming-kv=false? (not sure)
Devin: better: route low_kv_queue to kernels that prioritize memory locality and avoid heavy KV copy-outs. That reduces memcpy load.
Tony: can we simulate with the perf harness before rollout? Maria: yes I'll run a sweep with kv_admit_threshold_pct = [75,80,85,90] and low_kv_queue_token_cap = [64,128,256]
perf-bot: scheduled job 4970006799 (sweep), results ETA 2h
Maria: next steps: Linh implement admission filter + metrics, Devin add per-model kv ratio estimator, Tony add flags and rollout plan. I'll run perf harness and post results.
Tony: sounds good. @here if anyone else wants to weigh in on kernel routing alternatives.
Devin: one more note: include a microbenchmark for memcpy cost by kernel choice; we saw 30% CPU delta between kernels for same sequence lengths.
Linh: noted. I will also add CI guard that flags increase in memcpy time >10% during experiments.
Maria: thanks team, will update with sweep links and any surprising failures. :thumbsup:
